subject: Acme - Private observability: export safeguards & SIEM mapping
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-corp.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: secops@acme-corp.com
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment observability - SIEM field mapping & export constraints

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. As we move towards the private VPC deployment, SecOps needs a clear plan for how logs, metrics, and traces will leave our environment (if at all) and what scrubbing/encryption guarantees Redwood will provide. Two specific asks today:

1) A field-by-field mapping for Splunk (index names, event types, max size) so we can validate against our ingestion contracts. I attached the template.
2) A short write-up on how PII and sensitive headers are handled in the forwarder path — we need to be confident nothing sensitive is exfiltrated in clear text.

Also include any rate-limiting or burst controls (we have strict forwarding caps from our egress gateway). We have an upcoming audit (Nov 18) and will need evidence that the pipeline enforces those constraints.

Can you loop in the infra folks and share a proposed plan by Monday?

Best,
Jane
Security Operations
AcmeCorp

[attachment: acme_splunk_fields_map.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment observability - SIEM field mapping & export constraints

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear asks and the template. High-level plan below; I'll attach a concise PDF with the proposed network/egress layout and a first-pass field mapping.

Summary (tl;dr):
- Logs/metrics/traces will be forwarded from a customer-managed forwarder inside the VPC to Acme's Splunk HEC endpoint over TLS. No plaintext egress.
- PII scrubbing occurs at two points: (1) at the application-level exporters (recommended), and (2) at the forwarder (configurable regex scrub rules) for defense-in-depth.
- Rate limiting: Redwood forwarder supports token-bucket burst control; we'll recommend a steady-state throttle that matches your egress gateway (suggested default: 200 events/sec with a 5s burst).
- Traces: OTLP -> local collector -> OTLP/HTTP to your tracing backend (we can proxy through a private forwarder to centralize tokens). Sampling policy can be applied at the collector.

Open items for your team: exact Splunk HEC endpoints and token rotation cadence.

I'll schedule a 30-min technical sync with Marcus and Naomi for Monday AM to walk the mapping and firewall rules.

Actions:
- Marcus: propose firewall/egress rules and batching config (attached).
- Naomi: provide evidence pack template we can use for the audit.
- Stephanie (me): finalize the mapping PDF and send to you before EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-corp.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment observability - SIEM field mapping & export constraints

Hi all,

Technical notes / recommended configuration details for the forwarder and VPC egress:

1) Transport and authentication- HEC over HTTPS (TLS1.2+). Use client-side validation and pin the Acme root CA at the forwarder.
2) Network path- Forwarder runs in a dedicated telemetry subnet. Egress to Splunk via NAT gateway (preferred) or configured VPC endpoint. Allow outbound TCP 443 to your HEC host/IPs.
3) Firewall rules (security group egress)- 443 to splunk.hec.acme-corp.com (IP set provided in separate doc).
4) Scrubbing and field-mapping- Configure the forwarder to drop/replace these fields: user.email, user.ssn, request.headers.authorization. We recommend hashing user IDs (SHA-256) before export where possible. Example: transform user.email -> user.email_sha256.
5) Batching and backpressure- Use a 50–100ms batching window with max batch size 500 events; higher if your retention window supports burst smoothing. The forwarder exposes a health endpoint for our orchestrator to detect backpressure and switch to local buffering.
6) Token rotation and secrets- Store HEC tokens in your KMS and rotate every 30 days; our forwarder supports dynamic token reload via a sidecar secret volume.
7) Tracing- OTLP collector receives spans locally; configure tail-sampling to 1% for high-volume services and keep 100% for critical transaction types. Forward spans over HTTPS or gRPC; if you want centralized tokenization, we can route traces through a Redwood-managed proxy in your environment.

Event-rate sizing (rough):
- Baseline: 5k events/min across all services; batching parameters above should keep egress < 230 events/sec steady state.
- Peak bursts: our buffer + your NAT gateway should handle 3x bursts for up to 10 minutes. If you need higher, we can propose a short-term burst capacity change.

I'll bring a sample fluentd/otel config snippet to Monday's sync.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-corp.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: secops@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment observability - SIEM field mapping & export constraints

Thanks Marcus — that is helpful. Quick follow-ups:

- Can you confirm that request.headers.authorization will be stripped before any logs are buffered for outbound? We cannot accept auth tokens in any exported payload.
- For evidence: we need a short artifact showing the forwarder config and a sample of sanitized events (redacted) that we can present to auditors. Is that something Redwood can produce?
- Also the rate numbers look okay, but can you include an explicit egress SLA for events delivered to HEC (eg: 99.5% within 60s) so procurement can sign off.

If we can get those items today, we'll fold them into the audit submission.

Regards,
Jane

Subject: Re: Private deployment observability - SIEM field mapping & export constraints

Hi Jane — quick follow-up and checklist for the audit artifacts you asked for. Attached is a sanitized sample event (redacted) plus a short evidence pack template.

Confirmations:
- request.headers.authorization: removed at the forwarder ingress hook. The forwarder drops any header matching .*authorization.* before buffering.
- Sample artifact: included (sanitized_example_event.json) showing token fields removed and user.email hashed.
- SLA proposal: Redwood proposes event delivery SLA of 99.5% within 60s for standard telemetry. Exceptions: scheduled maintenance windows and forced-rate-limiting when downstream rejects traffic (we surface these in the console).

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- Wed 11/11: dry run (small dataset) — 1 hour window to validate scrubbing and HEC connectivity. Redwood to provide sanitized example and the config snippet to pre-install.
- Thu 11/12: full forwarder run with 2 hours of increased volume to observe backpressure behavior.
- Audit artifacts delivered 11/13 EOD if dry-run successful.

Action items:
- Acme: provide HEC endpoint + rotation cadence + list of IPs allowed for egress.
- Redwood: deliver sanitized sample and config snippet (attached).

Thanks — we’ll await the endpoint detail and will schedule the dry-run.

Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
